Average won-deal sales cycle

How we use it

We combine this with stage aging to identify approval or follow-up delays. Show the median and distribution when a small number of long deals distorts the average.

Transparent calculationSum of (closed-won timestamp − opportunity-created timestamp) in days ÷ number of closed-won opportunities
total won deal days420
closed won opportunities12

420 elapsed deal-days ÷ 12 won opportunities = a 35-day average.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Won deal segment and value
  • Sales owner and product
  • Opportunity-created cohort

Questions we investigate

  • Which stages delay successful deals?
  • Are a few long deals moving the average?
  • Did opportunity creation rules change?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Inspect stage timestamps and blockers.
  • Improve next-step ownership and approvals.
  • Review won-only speed with losses and open aging.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Sales operations lead
Monthly with median and range alongside the mean.

Required data

  • Won opportunity creation and closing timestamps
  • Deal segment and stage-transition records
  • Time-zone and elapsed-day policy

Read the measure with context

Zero won deals makes the average undefined. This excludes lost and still-open opportunities, so it is not the duration of every sales journey. Calendar days, working days, and lead-created starts produce different results and must be labeled.
